FIP.thesis_summary: A signed $1.52 billion sale of the Long Ridge power plant to MARA, awaiting only a change-of-control approval from the energy regulator, guided to close by the end of the third quarter of 2026 and cutting total debt from $3.8 billion to $2.4 billion; the shares at $4.23 sit near their fifty-two-week low against a $9.00 event-resolved value and a realistic $2.75 deal-break price.
FIP.dated_milestone: Change-of-control approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, application filed 8 May 2026 in docket EC26-92, guided by management to arrive in the middle of the third quarter of 2026, with the sale closing by 30 September 2026 on the seller's guidance. Nearest scheduled checkpoint: second-quarter 2026 results after the close on Wednesday 5 August 2026, with the conference call at 8:00 a.m. Eastern on Thursday 6 August 2026.

MARA's own 30 April 2026 announcement states Long Ridge contributes approximately $144 million of annualised adjusted EBITDA (second-half 2025 basis, reflecting the February 2025 hedge swaps and the June 2025 capacity payments) - i.e. the buyer underwrote roughly 10.5x, not 14x. FIP.dossier_note: Buy it now, and size it as a levered stub with a live event rather than as an arbitrage with a floor. The event is genuine. A definitive agreement was signed on 29 April 2026 to sell the Long Ridge power plant to MARA for about $1.52 billion, the regulatory application was filed on 8 May in docket EC26-92, the buyer cleared its bondholder consents in June, no financing contingency exists, and management has guided to approval by the middle of the third quarter. Nothing about it has fired, and the shares have actually fallen since the announcement, so none of the re-rating has been spent. At $4.23, close to the fifty-two-week low of $3.90 and against a high of $7.94, you are being paid to wait for a transaction that reduces total debt from $3.8 billion to $2.4 billion and saves about $30 million of interest a year, on a company whose surviving railroads grew earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation 31% year over year. There is no wash-out worth waiting for; this is the wash-out. Two things keep this from being the maximum-conviction version of this setup. The first is the floor. The entry carried into this review assumes $3.90 of downside protection, and that number is a chart level, not a recovery value. Book equity is negative $303.1 million, there is no net cash, operating cash flow was negative $69.4 million last quarter, and the filing's own liquidity assurance is expressly conditioned on this sale closing. A deal-break realistically prices the shares

VRDN.thesis_summary: The catalyst has already fired: the FDA approved Lumvoa (veligrotug-vvze) for thyroid eye disease on 26 June 2026, four days ahead of its 30 June target date and with a broader label than expected - and the stock is at $19.70 a month later, so the re-rating we were waiting to be paid for has been spent without paying, leaving roughly 52% upside to a $30 good-launch value against 57% downside to an $8.50 cash-based floor.
VRDN.dated_milestone: FDA approval granted 26 June 2026 (the target decision date was 30 June 2026) - fired, favourably and early, with the launch beginning the same week. Remaining calendar, none of it hard or binding: second-quarter results expected around 5 August 2026 (a stub month of launch revenue); management's guidance of broad insurance coverage within six to nine months of launch, pointing to roughly December 2026 through March 2027; a company-controlled approval filing for elegrobart targeted for the first quarter of 2027; and a European decision expected during 2027 on the application accepted in February 2026.
VRDN.kill_risk: [REFUTED] The catalyst has fired and nothing dated, binding or agency-controlled replaces it. Verified against the company's own 26 June 2026 release: the FDA approved Lumvoa (veligrotug-vvze) 'for the treatment of thyroid eye disease regardless of thyroid eye disease activity or duration', four days ahead of the 30 June 2026 PDUFA target action date, with no advisory committee, no complete response letter, and immediate launch -- physicians 'can prescribe Lumvoa tomorrow'. That is the best available version of the event this sleeve underwrote, and the tape refused it: the live quote is $19.70

VRDN.dossier_note:
This is a pass for now, and the reason is simple enough to state in one sentence: we were underwriting a dated regulatory decision, that decision arrived on 26 June 2026 - early, clean, and with a broader label than we expected - and the stock is at $19.70 a month later. When the best available outcome of a binary event does not pay, the market is pricing something the event did not address, and continuing to hold is no longer the trade we sized. It is a different trade wearing the old trade's clothes.

What the market is pricing is the 30 March 2026 data on elegrobart, the under-the-skin follow-on. That trial met its goal but at roughly 36 to 45 placebo-adjusted percentage points against about 64 for the approved infused drug, and the shares fell roughly a third that day and never recovered. The self-administered format is what was supposed to carry a chronic-disease franchise over a decade. A weaker version of it is a smaller company, and an approval for the infused drug does not repair that.

Two corrections to our own file, pulling in opposite directions. First, the balance sheet is much stronger than we carried: the company raised $350 million gross in May 2026 - shares at $17.00 plus 1.75% notes due 2032 - and collected a $75 million approval milestone from its royalty partner in late June, so cash is roughly $1.0 billion, not $600 million. The dilution risk we flagged as the way the floor breaks has already been taken, before the event, which is good treasury disciplin

EYPT.thesis_summary: The underwritten catalyst is spent. EyePoint's LUGANO pivotal Phase 3 — the readout the board dated to 2026-07-31 — fired on 2026-08-17 and MISSED its prespecified primary endpoint (change from baseline in BCVA vs on-label 2mg aflibercept) in the full randomized dataset. Non-inferiority appears only in an analysis the company itself labels ad hoc, excluding 9 of 211 DURAVYU patients (4%) who lost 15+ letters, against ZERO comparable cases in the control arm; the attached p=0.0096 is nominal and carries no regulatory weight. The tape resolved on the loss leg: $14.75 (2026-08-14) to $4.87 (2026-08-25 close, FMP), about -67%, with the 52-week low of $3.95 set the same week — i.e. BELOW the board's claimed $5.50 "floor," which was an assertion rather than an asset. The board's $37.50 target was RBC's pre-readout number; RBC withdrew it on 2026-08-18, cutting to $5 and downgrading to Sector Perform (Chardan $65 to $5, Jefferies $30 to $8, Jones $43 to $20, Citi to $17, JPMorgan to Neutral). A successor exists but is NOT the event we owned: LUCIA, the second identically designed pivotal, is fully enrolled with topline guided by the company to "the fourth quarter of 2026" (press reporting narrows it to October, not a company-fixed date), with an NDA in 1H 2027 contingent on it. That is a fresh, undated, unhedged binary in front of a near-certain financing — not the resolution of the dated event this seat was underwritten on.
EYPT.kill_risk: My load-bearing claim is that the edge is spent because LUGANO fired and failed and the successor is undated. Two credible refutations survive. (1) TIMING: the company's WRITTEN guidance is "Q4 2026," but sell-side and trade press since 2026-08-17 report LUCIA topline "expected in October." If EyePoint firms that into a fixed date, a re-underwritable dated binary sets up roughly six weeks after a FIRED exit — the classic sell-the-wreck-then-watch-it-double failure mode, and from a $4.87 base with ~$180m of cash behind it the win leg is a multiple, not a spread. My status is correct on today's record but has a short shelf life; re-poll before the sleeve treats this name as permanently dead. (2) VALUATION DIRECTION: at $408m cap against $180.5m cash and no borrowed debt, roughly $228m of program value is still priced in — this is NOT a max-fear print, so the risk to my $1.75 lose-leg is that it is far below where the tape would actually clear, while my 0.30 win_prob may itself be generous given XBI near a five-year high makes market-implied probabilities structurally rich. Residual risk cuts both ways: the floor is too low for a tactical mark and the entry is not cheap enough for a fresh binary.

EYPT.dossier_note:
FIRED, verified three ways. EyePoint's 2026-08-17 release (globenewswire + investors.eyepoint.bio; 8-K accession 0001193125-26-353308), Reuters 2026-08-17 ("EyePoint's eye drug misses main goal in late-stage trial"), and the tape ($14.75 on 08-14 to $4.87 on 08-25, -67%) all agree: LUGANO did not meet the prespecified primary. The board's date (2026-07-31) was already wrong pre-fire by 17 days.

WHY THE $37.50 CANNOT BE REPRODUCED. It was RBC's pre-readout target, withdrawn 2026-08-18 (cut to $5, downgrade to Sector Perform). Same-day broker resets: Chardan $65->$5, Jefferies $30->$8, Jones $43->$20, Citi ->$17, JPMorgan ->Neutral (pre-miss Street average was $38.58). The board's target had no independent derivation behind it — it was a single withdrawn sell-side print.

WIN LEG = $17.00 (LUCIA-conditional, NOT a mark on the fired event). The surviving post-cut targets ($5/$5/$8/$17/$20) are blended numbers that already carry LUCIA risk; a clean LUCIA primary win should clear the top of that band but stays far below $37.50 because one-win/one-miss on the prespecified endpoint is a materially weaker NDA than two wins, and the July-2024 cGMP Warning Letter on the Watertown YUTIQ line sits on the CMC path for a company whose only asset is a manufactured drug-eluting insert (nuance vs the board skeptic: the 10-Q states the required corrective and preventive action plan was FULLY EXECUTED, so this is an overhang, not a confirmed open deficiency). $17.00 = Citi's post-cut mark, below Jones' $20; deliberately taken as the conservative end.

LOSE LEG = $1.75, from the balance sheet, not assertion. 6/30/26 (10-Q filed 2026-08-05): cash + ST investments $180.472m, ZERO borrowed debt, $22.367m finance-lease obligations, payables + accrued $39.3m, equity $166.4m, 83.84m shares out. July ATM added ~1,208,718 shares (~$17m; corroborated — Q2 ATM was 1,429,047 sh at $14.16 wtd avg = $20.2m gross, matching Q2 cash-flow common stock issuance of $20.178m). Realized burn: Q1 op CF -$80.5m, Q2 -$62.3m = $142.9m in H1, roughly $71m/quarter. Carrying to a 12/31/26 readout: $180.5m + $17m - ~$105m (two tapering quarters) = ~$92m, less $22.4m leases = ~$70m net, over ~85m shares = ~$0.82/share of hard net cash. Adding residual DME optionality (COMO/CAPRI fully enrolled, 480+ patients, topline Q4 2027) and YUTIQ gets a busted-single-asset clearing price of $1.50-2.00; I take $1.75.

RUNWAY DISCREPANCY WORTH THE CRO'S ATTENTION. The company guides $180m as runway "into Q4 2027," which implies about $33m/quarter — less than HALF the realized H1 2026 rate of ~$71m/quarter. At the realized rate $180m is ~2.5 quarters (into roughly Q1 2027). The guided runway therefore requires a >50% spend taper or further ATM issuance, and the ATM is already routine — the next tranche prints near a third of the $14.16/$14.44 levels at which the last two were sold.

WIN_PROB 0.30. LUCIA is the same molecule, same insert, same comparator, same endpoint. The bull case is that LUGANO's miss was an artifact of 9 of 211 DURAVYU patients losing 15+ letters "unrelated to wet AMD." But 9/211 versus 0/211 in control is not a chance imbalance (Fisher exact approx. p=0.004 two-sided) — the likelier reading is drug- or device-related, which recurs in an identically designed trial. That is the single strongest reason 0.60 cannot carry over.

EV CHECK, for transparency only (sizing is the Director's): 0.30 x $17.00 + 0.70 x $1.75 = $5.10 + $1.23 = $6.33 against $4.87 spot. Positive on paper — but attached to an UNDATED event, unhedged, with a dilutive raise standing in front of it. catalyst_live=false is the operative field here; these axes exist so the seat is not adjudicated off a dead $37.50/$5.50 pair.

TAKEOUT LENS — NO LIFT APPLIED. The 2026 record-pace biotech M&A cohort (37 takeouts >=$1B YTD, $216B) is late-stage, commercially-ready assets; a failed prespecified primary disqualifies EYPT from that cohort today, so strategic scarcity is currently negative, not positive. The retina precedent that would frame a conditional bid is Astellas/Iveric Bio ($5.9B, April 2023) — but it is three years stale and was a clean pre-approval asset, so it does not carry provenance strong enough to lift the win leg, and I have not lifted it. Any takeout interest is contingent on a LUCIA win, is undated, and is explicitly NOT treated as a milestone.

REGIME CAVEAT. XBI near a five-year high means market-implied win probabilities are rich and old max-fear floor prints are stale-low. Cutting the other way: $408m cap on $180.5m cash means ~$228m of program value is STILL priced in post-crash, so this is not a capitulation print, and the gap between $4.87 and my $1.75 lose-leg is the honest measure of how much LUCIA optimism the tape is already carrying.

LZM.dated_milestone: One real calendar item and one real deadline, neither of which is the catalyst itself. (1) First-half 2026 interim financial results on 29 July 2026, with an investor webcast at 10:00 a.m. New York time hosted by chief executive Chris Showalter and chief financial officer Ingo Hofmaier -- confirmed by the company on 27 July 2026 and verified today. This is a disclosure venue at which management must either produce the concluded process or explain a second missed milestone; it resolves nothing by itself. (2) The Taurus senior secured bridge matures on 31 July 2027, which is the outer bound on how long this can drift -- a deadline that works for the lender, not the shareholder. The catalyst proper -- the strategic-partner transaction -- has no announced date, and the two gates behind it, the Framework Agreement amendment with the Tanzanian government and the power supply agreements, are undated as well.

LZM.dossier_note:
This is a real event on a broken clock, and the discipline that makes this funnel work is the discipline to say so.

Start with what is true. Kabanga is a genuine tier-one orebody -- among the largest and highest-grade development-ready nickel sulfide deposits anywhere, in the cheapest quarter of the cost curve, with an independently prepared study value of $1.58 billion against a $298 million company. The sale process is real, competitive and advanced, corroborated by a wire-service leak specific enough that the company had to respond on 8 June 2026. If it concludes at a defensible fraction of study value, $7.00 is a defensible number and this roughly doubles.

Now what is not true. This is not a defined-risk event position, and treating it as one is the error the catalyst discipline exists to prevent. There is no date: the guided mid-2026 build decision lapsed silently, and 'concluding shortly' was said eighty-nine days ago. There is nothing binding: no agreement, no outside date, no regulator on a clock, no contractual payout. Two hard prerequisites -- a sovereign fiscal amendment and a utility power agreement -- are themselves undated, and one of them cannot be scheduled by anybody. And the floor our board carried at $2.60 is folklore. There is no net cash beneath this price (the company is $38 million net borrowed), no deal-break level, no recovery claim -- only a secured lender whose collateral is the shares in the project company itself and whose facility has reportedl

DDL.thesis_summary: Signed SPA (5 Feb 2026): Meituan subsidiary Two Hearts Investments buys Dingdong's China business for US$717M cash; with the pre-closing draw right (up to US$280M before 31 Aug 2026) total cash proceeds run up to US$997M, ~ $4.60/ADS gross vs $2.48 traded. Shareholders approved 27 Mar 2026; the company INTENDS (board absolute discretion, not binding) to return >=90% of post-closing cash via buybacks/dividends. Gating condition is SAMR anti-monopoly clearance (undated by regime design); contractual long-stop ~5 Feb 2027 (12 months from signing, extendable by mutual consent). Verified UNFIRED as of 4 Aug 2026: no clearance, no closing, no company communication since 21 May 2026, no SEC filing since 26 May 2026. Near-term observable: Q2 results (~20 Aug 2026 per aggregators, undated by company) will show whether the <=$280M draw was exercised before the 31 Aug soft date. Buyer break fees US$150M/US$75M tiered; company fee US$75M.
DDL.kill_risk: The single most load-bearing claim - that closing cash actually reaches shareholders - does not fully survive: the 27 Mar 2026 AGM resolution is EMPOWERING, not binding (board may deploy cash 'in its absolute discretion'), the 10 Feb release carries express no-assurance language, and the company is founder-controlled with super-voting shares. If the deal closes but the board returns only ~half the cash, value is ~ $2.41/ADS - BELOW the $2.48 tape; the position is a governance bet stacked on a regulatory bet. Secondary: SAMR clearance is undated and could run past the (extendable) Feb 2027 long-stop; passing 31 Aug 2026 without the draw is not disprovable evidence of trouble but would remove the near-term confirm.

THRM.dated_milestone: Verified: United States antitrust review completed with early termination of the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period granted at 11:25 a.m. Eastern Time on 26 March 2026; international regulatory clearance also secured. Financing committed at $800 million, with a $550 million five-year revolving credit facility signed 29 June 2026. Registration statement filed 2 July 2026. Closing guided by management on the 23 July 2026 earnings call to early in the fourth quarter of 2026, which is a guided window and not a fixed date. The shareholder special meeting has no announced date and cannot be scheduled until the registration statement is declared effective. A private tax ruling from the Internal Revenue Service remains outstanding.
THRM.thesis_summary: The United States antitrust clearance this position was built on already happened, on 26 March 2026, and the stock has since risen roughly 25% to $42.07 against a $44 target and a $30 floor, leaving about 5% of upside against about 29% of downside.

LBTYK.thesis_summary: Liberty Global is a holding company trading at ~$10.64 (LBTYK, ~341m shares, ~$3.63bn market cap) whose resolving event is the spin-off of Ziggo Group — VodafoneZiggo (Netherlands) plus Telenet (Belgium), 13m customers, EUR6.6bn revenue — to be listed on Euronext Amsterdam in 2027, with Liberty Global distributing its 90% to shareholders tax-free for US holders. The structural precondition is now DONE: on 3 August 2026 the company completed the purchase of Vodafone's 50% of VodafoneZiggo for EUR1.0bn cash plus a 10% Ziggo Group stake, so there is no longer a JV partner, no approval contingency and no financing condition standing between here and the listing. The trade is the holdco discount closing: on management's own Q2 marks, guided year-end corporate cash of ~$2.0bn ($5.87/sh) plus the Liberty Growth portfolio at $2.9bn FMV ($8.50/sh) equals $14.37/sh with every telecom asset — 90% of Ziggo Group, 50% of Virgin Media O2, VM Ireland — carried at zero. The listing is the mechanism that forces the market to mark the telecom stub, exactly as the 2024 Sunrise spin did. It is genuinely idiosyncratic: nothing about the outcome depends on the tape, only on whether Liberty Global executes a distribution it has already restructured itself to make. What it is NOT is dated. There is no record date, no listing prospectus, no scheduled shareholder vote; guidance was tightened to "as early as mid-2027" in the 24 July Q2 release and then restated as plain "2027" in the 3 August completion release, and the board retains the right to abandon.
LBTYK.kill_risk: The most load-bearing claim in the thesis is that ~$2.0bn of holdco cash underwrites the downside. It is a forecast, not a balance, and I cannot bridge it from the live record. The Q2 10-Q reconciles exactly to the skeptic's read: consolidated cash $2,418.6m at 30 June 2026, of which only $1,610.1m "represented available liquidity at the corporate level" and $808.5m sits inside the Telenet and VM Ireland borrowing groups. The EUR1.0bn (~$1.15bn) Vodafone payment went out on 3 August, leaving roughly $0.46bn of corporate cash plus $76m of separately-managed-account investments. Getting to $2.0bn by 31 December therefore needs ~$1.5bn of further H2 inflows, and the disposals named to supply it — the 50% Wyre stake (guided only to year-end 2026 or Q1 2027), the VodafoneZiggo towers, Belgian and Dutch property, EUR1.2-1.4bn in total — are described in the company's own 3 August release as proceeds that "will be used to retire debt" at the subsidiaries, not upstreamed to the holding company. I could not determine from any primary source whether the Vodafone payment was funded from holdco cash or from the new Benelux debt (Wyre drew EUR2.71bn of a EUR4.35bn facility, upstreaming ~EUR2.38bn to Telenet, which then repaid EUR2.12bn of its own 2028 maturities); the two readings differ by more than a dollar a share on the floor. Compounding it: ~$340m of the $1.2bn of year-to-date "monetizations" is an asset-backed loan secured on the Wyre stake — borrowed money encumbering the very asset the next checkpoint depends on selling — and the 10-Q states no repurchase program is authorized for 2026, so there is no company bid to defend the discount before the spin. Second-order but real: the resolving event carries no binding date and the 3 August release dropped the "as early as mid-2027" qualifier the Q2 release had added, which is the shape a quiet slip takes before it is announced as one.

KDP.thesis_summary: KDP is separating its coffee business (Global Coffee Co., which includes US Coffee plus the JDE Peet's assets acquired 1 Apr 2026 for $18.4B) from the North American refreshment-beverage business via a tax-free spin-off targeted for "early 2027" — reaffirmed in the Q2 release of 6 Aug 2026 and the 10-Q of 10 Aug 2026. The trade in KDP common is a sum-of-the-parts re-rating on completion, NOT an index-flow trade: KDP is the RemainCo, retains the ticker, listing and index seat, and index funds are obliged to keep these shares. Whatever forced flow the transaction creates lands on the SpinCo, a security that does not yet exist. The parts are genuinely mismatched — a ~30%-margin US beverage franchise growing sales 10.0% and segment OI 11.9% sits inside the same multiple as a coffee arm whose adjusted OI fell 24.7% y/y on green-coffee costs and tariffs — and the blended entity trades at ~10.6x 2027E EBITDA against parts worth ~11.5-12x. The event itself is real and unfired but carries no binding date, no Form 10 on file as of 25 Aug 2026, no board approval of the distribution, and the company's own stated conditions include "appropriate leverage levels at each company, and supportive market conditions."
KDP.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that completion unlocks an unpaid-for SoP re-rating. Three live facts cut against it. (1) The parts are largely already paid for: sell-side consensus PT is $37.75 (median $38, high $42) versus my $38.50, so the SoP is the consensus view, not a variant one — and the stock is already +12.6% over its 200d MA and 3.9% off its 52-week high, so the discount has been narrowing without the event. (2) The company conditions separation timing on "supportive market conditions" and on reaching appropriate leverage at each entity — by its own language the event is tape-dependent, not idiosyncratic, which is disqualifying for an event-driven sleeve; a risk-off tape both delays the catalyst and de-rates the stock at the same time (correlated, not independent). (3) Execution wobble is real and unresolved: no Form 10 on file at 25 Aug 2026 (a US distribution cannot occur until one is filed and effective, normally 2-4 months ahead), the board has not approved the distribution, and the designated Global Coffee CEO left at end-July 2026 with no successor named — the SpinCo has no CEO roughly five months from its own target window. Secondary: my CoffeeCo leg at 9.5x may itself be generous — US Coffee adjusted OI is running −24.7% y/y and a standalone, levered coffee company carrying green-coffee and tariff cost pass-through could clear at 8x or less, which alone removes ~$2/sh from the target.

CAPR.dossier_note: My recommendation is to pass for now, and to say plainly why, because the reason matters more than the conclusion. This position was entered as a defined-risk bet on a dated event: a stock at $19.44, a target of $52, and a floor of $7.00 that was supposed to bound the loss if the regulator said no. Three of those four numbers have failed. The date was mislabelled -- 29 July is an advisory panel, not a decision; the decision comes on 22 August. The price is $6.45 this morning against $19.70 at Friday's close. And the floor has been breached before the event has even occurred, which tells us it was never a floor. It was a guess at where the stock would settle after a refusal, and the market repriced straight through it on the mere publication of the regulator's reasoning. The verified floor, built from the balance sheet, is roughly $3.60 a share of net cash -- about $209M after four months of burn against 57.66 million shares -- and it erodes by roughly $0.20 a share every month. That is 44% below the current price, not above it. The whole architecture of this trade rested on a floor that does not exist where it was recorded. What is left is a coin flip priced at roughly fair value. My probability-weighted estimate is $7.00 a share against a $6.45 quote: an 8% expected return in exchange for an 88% chance of losing close to 40% within four weeks, in a position that cannot be hedged at sensible cost two days before a public vote. That is not the trade this funnel exists to find.

ANNX.thesis_summary: Annexon carries one dated in-window gate, but it is not the event the board underwrote. On 12 Aug 2026 the company replaced the guided Month-15 ARCHER II TOPLINE readout with an independent Data Monitoring Committee ASSESSMENT of the Month-15 primary endpoint, still guided to Q4 2026, and added a Month-24 dual primary. Verbatim: "An independent Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) will assess the primary endpoint of the overall study at Month 15, and the Company expects to report the DMC's assessment in the fourth quarter of 2026. Following this assessment, the DMC may recommend that the ARCHER II overall study has met its Month 15 primary endpoint, enabling the planned analysis of the trial's two sub-studies, with results anticipated in the first quarter of 2027; or it may recommend that the study continues until the Month 24 primary endpoint analysis." Management confirmed on the 19 Aug 2026 call that no patient-level data comes in Q4 2026, and that the DMC may also declare futility. So the Q4 2026 print is a masked three-way gate (met / continue / futile), not a two-sided data binary: the win branch delivers direction without magnitude and defers the numbers to Q1 2027; the modal miss branch delivers "continue," which does not resolve and pushes the real verdict to trial completion in Q3 2027. The second board leg — a 31 Dec 2026 FDA approval decision for tanruprubart in Guillain-Barre — does not exist: the BLA is still only guided for Q4 2026 SUBMISSION (already slipped once from H1-2025 guidance), so no PDUFA date can exist and the earliest US verdict is late 2027; the EU MAA has been under EMA review since 8 Jan 2026 with no disclosed opinion date. The tradeable proposition is therefore: pay $5.06 for a masked committee vote inside ~4 months, backed by ~$0.80/share of net cash falling to ~$0.42/share by the print, against a live ATM and 500m authorized shares.
ANNX.kill_risk: My own load-bearing claim is that "a dated, binding binary survives in Q4 2026." It only half survives refutation. The guide is a QUARTER, not a date, and it is a sponsor disclosure commitment about a third-party committee's meeting — there is no statutory clock like a PDUFA forcing it. This management has already slipped the tanruprubart BLA from H1-2025 to Q4-2026 and restructured this very endpoint once (May topline guide -> Aug DMC guide), so a slide of the DMC report into Q1 2027 is an ordinary outcome, not a tail. Worse, the modal branch is non-informative by design: "the study continues to Month 24" tells the holder nothing about effect size, direction, or safety, and the tape will mark it as a miss without ever confirming one. The honest residual risk is that a holder can sit through 31 Dec 2026 and receive either nothing at all or an unresolving "continue," while ~$18.4m/month burns, the ATM is live, and the 500m-share authority (granted at the 11 June 2026 annual meeting, not pending) is available — i.e. the position can lose most of the gap to the floor without the binary ever having resolved. Second-order: $150m of the "into 2028" runway is Oxford milestone/discretionary tranches contingent on the registrational programs, so it is least available exactly on the branch where it is most needed.

CLVT.thesis_summary: The event this seat was underwriting has resolved. On 2026-07-06 Clarivate signed a definitive agreement to sell substantially all of its Life Sciences & Healthcare segment to Altaris for $600M ($500M cash at close, $25M deferred to TSA completion, $75M seller note), with close expected by year-end 2026 subject to regulatory approvals. The board dossier's premise -- "in active discussions since Feb 24 2026 with no signed agreement, no buyer, no price" -- is stale by a month. The edge was spent, and spent adversely: CLVT ran to $2.59 on 2026-07-02 into the leak, printed $2.44 on the announcement, and has bled to $1.94, a 25% drawdown from the pre-announcement mark, through an EPS beat on 2026-07-29. The reason is arithmetic, not sentiment: LS&H went at roughly 5.0x EBITDA while the whole capital structure sits at 4.0x net leverage, so the sale is essentially leverage-neutral (4.00x pre, 3.98x post). What remains is not an event -- it is a levered low-growth stub trading at ~5.4x pro-forma EBITDA whose upside requires a multiple re-rate no dated catalyst delivers. That is a value-book question, not a Basket 13 one.
CLVT.dated_milestone: Close of the LS&H divestiture to Altaris, guided "by year-end 2026" (i.e. on/before 2026-12-31), conditioned on customary closing conditions including regulatory approvals and expiration of applicable waiting periods. Company-guided window, not a regulator-set hard date. Residual only: CLVT holders receive no consideration at close -- the $500M retires notes -- so the close moves cash, not price.
CLVT.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim in the $4.20 target is that RemainCo re-rates from today's ~5.4x to 7.0x pro-forma EV/EBITDA. Nothing dated forces that, and the live record argues against it. (1) Deleveraging is illusory -- net leverage goes 4.00x to 3.98x through the sale; the balance sheet is no safer on 2027-01-01 than it is today. (2) Growth does not support a re-rate: reaffirmed FY26 ACV organic growth is only 2.0-3.0%. (3) Management is marking its own assets down -- Q2 carried a $221.7M goodwill impairment inside a $268.6M net loss. (4) Senior turnover is running hot: CFO Jonathan Collins out (Michael Easton effective 2026-08-08), IP segment president Mourad out (Simon Webster from 2026-06-10). (5) The tape has rejected every positive print -- an EPS beat of $0.19 vs $0.17 on 2026-07-29 was followed by $2.15 -> $2.01 -> $1.98 -> $1.94. Structurally the bear case is that AI substitution erodes the Web of Science / Derwent data franchises, which is precisely why the market pays 5.4x and not 12x like unlevered info-services peers. The stub is the risk: at 3.98x leverage, one turn of multiple compression puts the equity at $1.42 and half a turn of EBITDA erosion (~$890M to ~$800M) at 5.0x puts it near $0.30. Deal-break risk is a live tail too, and it is asymmetric -- closing is priced, a regulatory failure is not.

SVRA.thesis_summary: Savara is a single-asset binary on the FDA approval of MOLBREEVI (molgramostim inhalation solution, inhaled recombinant GM-CSF delivered via PARI's eFlow nebulizer) for autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis - which would be the first and only approved therapy in the indication. Efficacy is settled: IMPALA-2 hit its primary endpoint (change in hemoglobin-adjusted %-predicted DLCO at Wk24) and multiple secondaries, with LS-mean DLCO +11.6pp vs +4.7pp placebo at Wk48 (p<0.001) and SGRQ-T -11.5 vs -4.9 at Wk24 (p=0.007), published and presented through ATS 2026. BLA is under Priority Review with Fast Track, Breakthrough and Orphan designations and NO advisory committee. The resolving event is the PDUFA action date, which is idiosyncratic and forward-dated - but it is 2026-11-22, not the board's 2026-08-22: the FDA deemed Savara's responses to information requests a major amendment and extended the review three months (announced 2026-04-15). The residual question is not whether the drug works; it is whether the manufacturing/device dossier clears, in a program that has already been refused-to-file once on exactly that.
SVRA.kill_risk: CMC/drug-device manufacturing, not efficacy, is the live failure mode - and it has already bitten this program once. Refuting my own load-bearing claim ("efficacy is settled so approval is near-certain"): the FDA issued a Refusal to File on 2025-05-27 because the March-2025 BLA was not complete enough for substantive review, specifically requesting additional Chemistry, Manufacturing and Controls data (stock -32% that day, 25M shares, $2.93 to $1.94). The file was only resubmitted in Dec-2025 and filed in Feb-2026. Now, mid-review, FDA information requests have again triggered a major amendment and a three-month clock reset. For an inhaled biologic dependent on a third-party device partner (PARI eFlow), the approvable gate is CMC/device/facility inspection, and that gate has a demonstrated history of catching this sponsor. Note also that "the FDA did not cite any safety, efficacy, or manufacturing concerns" is the company's characterisation of correspondence, not an FDA statement of approvability - and management's regulatory-readiness disclosures are themselves the subject of a securities class action filed Sept-2025 (Rosen, E.D. Pa.) over the prior BLA. A CMC CRL is resolvable in 6-12 months but destroys the dated event and, from a $1.09B market cap now substantially priced for approval, costs far more than the RTF did off a ~$490M base.

IMXI.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is "WU still intends to close at $16.00" - and the live record materially weakens it. WU's 2026-07-30 Q2 missed badly (adj EPS $0.31 vs $0.42 est and $0.42 LY, adj operating margin -4pp, Americas retail deteriorating, stock $8.47 on an ~11-13% yield). IMXI itself has deteriorated far more since signing: Q1-26 revenue $121.95M vs $144.31M (-15.5%), net income $0.51M vs $7.77M (-93%), principal sent -11.4%, operating cash flow swung to -$37.4M, revolver drawn $240.8M against a $369M market cap. So WU has both motive and an option point: it can decline to trigger the final outside-date extension on 2026-08-10 and press for a lower price on an asset now worth conspicuously less than at signing. Crucially, the $27.3M reverse fee is payable only under specified ANTITRUST restraints - HSR cleared in Oct-2025 - so a failure driven by a state money-transmitter regulator likely pays IMXI NOTHING; holders eat the full break to standalone value. RARE.thesis_summary: Ultragenyx faces a hard, dated FDA decision on UX111 (rebisufligene etisparvovec) for Sanfilippo syndrome type A on 19 September 2026 — 25 days out, unfired, not slipped, and resolving purely on its own regulatory facts. The resubmission was accepted 2 April 2026 after a July 2025 complete response letter that was confined to manufacturing information and facility inspection observations, not to whether the drug works. There is no approved therapy for MPS IIIA anywhere in the world. Approval odds are genuinely good — roughly 75% — and a second rare pediatric disease priority review voucher, worth $150-195M on live comparable sales, comes with it. What has changed since the board wrote this dossier is not the event but what the event is worth. On 19 August the company won its first-ever gene therapy approval (GENGLYCOS, four days ahead of its 23 August action date) and took a voucher in hand, and the stock is worth $0.23 more today than the day before. The market has already run this experiment and paid almost nothing for the answer, which is why the win leg is $28 rather than $30 — and why the $18 "floor" the board carried is a price memory, not a floor, on a balance sheet with negative equity and $1.08B of net debt.
RARE.kill_risk: The residual capture on approval may be zero, not the +$2.28 I have underwritten. The single load-bearing claim in my thesis is that a 19 September approval is not yet fully in the price. The live record argues the opposite and it argues it twice. On 19-20 August the company delivered a strictly larger surprise than the one still on file — a first-ever gene therapy approval, delivered four days EARLY, carrying a voucher worth $150-195M — and the stock opened $28.39, printed its high at $28.50, and closed $25.32 down 10.8% on 3.84M shares. Two weeks earlier a record quarter produced the identical shape: open $28.48 was the day's high, close $24.93, down 12.5%. In both cases the open was the high. Net durable repricing from the August approval plus the voucher is +$0.23 a share. If the market pays roughly nothing for a delivered approval and a voucher in hand, it may pay roughly nothing for a second, better-telegraphed one, and the whole positive expected value rests on a re-rating the tape has just refused twice at the exact level the target must clear. Secondary and unresolved: the July 2025 letter cited observations from inspections of facilities, plural, and UX111 needs both Ultragenyx's Bedford, MA site and Andelyn Biosciences in Columbus, OH. The August approval validated Bedford. Andelyn is an independent contract manufacturer, separately inspectable, and was not cleared by it — so the manufacturing objection is half-answered, not answered.

The event is real and the odds are good; the payoff shape is the problem, and which frame the CRO holds this in decides whether it is positive expected value at all. That fork is the deliverable here, not a verdict.

The 2026 late-stage biotech M&A regime is genuinely hot, and Ultragenyx has the profile in some respects: five approved products, $730-760M guided 2026 revenue, Crysvita at $156M in the quarter, path to profitability in 2027, a deep ultra-rare franchise. CMCSA.thesis_summary: Comcast announced 2026-06-29 (8-K Ex-99.1) its intention to separate into two public companies via a tax-free spin-off of NBCUniversal + Sky, "expected to be completed in approximately one year" (i.e. ~mid-2027). RemainCo = domestic broadband/wireless/business services on the 65m-home converged network (Michael Angelakis CEO); SpinCo = Universal parks/studios, NBC/Telemundo, Peacock, Bravo and Sky (Mike Cavanagh CEO). The trade is a sum-of-the-parts re-rate: the consolidated entity trades at ~4.85x EV/EBITDA (EV $169.9B on $87.2B cap + $82.7B Q2-2026 net debt, over ~$35B FY26E adjusted EBITDA), while the live comps are CHTR at 5.70x and DIS at 10.81x EV/EBITDA TTM. Marking the parts at 5.5x / 7.5x on 2027E gets ~$34/sh vs $24.56 spot. Carry is paid by the $0.33/qtr dividend declared 2026-07-23 (5.4% yield, covered ~3.5x by H1-26 FCF of $8.5B).
CMCSA.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is "the parts re-rate." Three live facts cut against it. (1) Comcast just ran this experiment: the Versant spin closed 2026-01-02 and the stub went from a $32.86 52-wk high to a $21.28 low - a spin at this issuer has already failed once in seven months to re-rate the remainder. (2) The EBITDA base is eroding faster than the multiple is likely to expand: Q2-26 residential C&P adjusted EBITDA fell 8.0% y/y, domestic broadband revenue -5.5%, 167k broadband subs lost in the quarter, and total adjusted EBITDA fell 5.3% y/y even pro forma for Versant/Sky-Germany. A 23-month hold against a -5%/yr base eats most of a one-turn re-rate. (3) The Disney-multiple analogue is structurally blocked: the 8-K states NBCUniversal will carry "the same dual-class share structure as Comcast" (Roberts control retained) and Comcast keeps up to 19.9% of SpinCo to monetize over time - a governance discount plus a stated overhang, against a single-class DIS comp. Deal risk is also non-trivial and self-declared: final board approval, tax opinions, regulatory approvals and financing are all still outstanding, with "no assurance that the proposed transaction will be completed." Finally, the driver is only semi-idiosyncratic - completion resolves on company facts, but the realized value depends on where the tape chooses to multiple cable and legacy media in mid-2027.

The January 2026 interim already showed an 85% median hsCRP reduction with 94% of subjects driven below 2 mg/L and no infection signal, so the expansion is largely CONFIRMATORY on the biomarker rather than discovery. The event is idiosyncratic (resolves on GLUE's own trial data), the balance sheet is not a variable ($666M cash+ST investments at 3/31/26, guided runway into 2029), and the option value sits in three additional shots: MRT-6160 (VAV1) partnered to Novartis with multiple Phase 2 starts pending, MRT-2359 (GSPT1) entering Phase 2 in mCRPC in Q3 2026, and a CCNE1 IND in H2 2026. GLUE fell ~28-30% on that read-across (roughly $24 on 1 July to $15.38 today, versus a $20.78 50-day average). ZEUS does not invalidate GLUE's own readout, but it devalues its payoff: the surrogate GLUE is about to report on is the same surrogate ZEUS just dissociated from clinical outcome. The catalyst survives; the prize behind it does not survive intact.
GLUE.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim in the thesis is that a positive expanded GFORCE-1 hsCRP readout is a value-creating de-risking event. The live record refutes it directly: ZEUS (2026-07-31) showed that TOTAL suppression of the IL-6/hsCRP axis produced MACE HR 0.99 in exactly the elevated-CVD-risk population GLUE is enrolling. GLUE's readout measures the same surrogate, so the event can resolve maximally positive and still produce no re-rate, or a "so what" fade. Two further live risks: (1) IL-1-pathway blockade carries a class serious-infection signal, seen on active drug in ZEUS, and a larger/longer expansion cohort is materially more likely to surface it than the small interim was; (2) the H2 2026 window is soft and the 2026-08-06 Q2 call could re-scope or defer the elevated-atherosclerotic-risk Phase 2, which would convert this to SLIPPED. Bristol Myers Squibb is the obvious name and the WEAKEST one: it handed IMA401 back effective 12-Dec-2024, so the large-pharma validation on the bispecific franchise is already gone. Conclusion: the takeout leg is undated optionality that becomes live only AFTER a SUPRAME win, at which point it is embedded in the re-rate — it is not a milestone, it does not extend or substitute for one, and it does not lift $14.00 today. It is, however, where the board's $20 was implicitly coming from; a post-win takeout at a 40-60% premium to standalone reaches $19-22, which is a CONDITIONAL CAP, not fair value.

5) INSTRUMENT NOTE (fact, not a trade view): the board's own instrument line already flags that options carry a full 9-12 month binary IV load. That was written when the binary was expected to resolve in 2026; after the slip the option path now spans roughly four quarters MORE than the board assumed. Tradeability is the CRO's call — recording the fact only.

VNDA.thesis_summary: Vanda ($5.23, 60.1M sh, $315M cap) carries a hard, forward-dated FDA binary: the imsidolimab (anti-IL-36R mAb) BLA for generalized pustular psoriasis, PDUFA target action date 2026-12-12, accepted for filing 2026-02-25. The pivotal record is clean and public — GEMINI-1 met its primary endpoint (53.3% vs 13.3% GPPPGA 0/1 at wk4, p=0.0131), published in NEJM Evidence 2026-04-28, with orphan designation in the US, EU (2026-07-16) and Japan (2026-05-27). The event is idiosyncratic (a single agency decision on its own dossier) and unfired. It sits on top of a real commercial base — 2026 revenue guided $240-290M, Fanapt +26% in Q1 — that the market currently values at roughly 0.47x sales after netting cash, so very little imsidolimab value is embedded in the tape. The offsetting fact is a balance sheet running down fast: cash+ST investments fell $61.5M in Q1-26 alone, to $202.3M, and management has guided 2026 burn above 2025's.
VNDA.kill_risk: Financing gap ahead of the event. Net cash/share has collapsed from the ~$6.75 the board itself cited in 2024 when rejecting Cycle Pharma's $8.00 cash bid, to $3.37 at 2026-03-31 — Q1-26 alone consumed $61.5M of cash+ST investments, and management guided 2026 burn above 2025. A registration statement went effective 2026-05-05 (EFFECT, CIK 1347178), i.e. the shelf is armed. An equity raise between the 2026-08-05 Q2 print and the 2026-12-12 PDUFA would dilute the win leg before it pays, and every quarter of burn erodes the downside floor by roughly $0.58/sh of net cash. Second, independent risk: imsidolimab is Vanda's FIRST biologic BLA, so CMC and pre-approval-inspection failure — the modal CRL cause and entirely invisible from the efficacy record above — is not covered by the strong GEMINI-1 result. The historical "Vanda always loses at FDA" bear case (Hetlioz jet-lag CRL 2026-01-08, tradipitant gastroparesis) is the weaker objection and I discount it: FDA approved BYSANTI on 2026-02-20 and NEREUS in 2026, two on-time wins this year.

Vanda's 2026-07-29 press release sets 2026-08-05 as the Q2-2026 EARNINGS release date (after close, call 4:30pm ET). The scan appears to have grabbed the next calendar event and mislabeled it as the approval decision. The actual FDA action date under this driver is the imsidolimab GPP PDUFA of 2026-12-12 (BLA acceptance PR 2026-02-25, reconfirmed in the Q1 release 2026-05-06). VNDA.dossier_note:

Q1-26 (3/31/26) balance sheet: cash $54.0M + ST inv $148.3M = $202.3M ($3.37/sh); LT inv $0.4M; total debt $13.1M (finance leases only, no funded debt). Net cash $189.6M = $3.15/sh. Current EV = 314.5 - 189.6 = $124.9M, i.e. 0.47x the $265M midpoint of 2026 revenue guidance ($240-290M incl. $10-30M NEREUS). The market is pricing the burn, not the revenue line.

BURN PATH (drives both legs). Cash+ST inv: Q2-25 $325.6M -> Q3-25 $293.8M (-31.8) -> Q4-25 $263.8M (-30.0) -> Q1-26 $202.3M (-61.5). Q1-26 doubled the 2025 run-rate; management guided 2026 burn above 2025. I mark Q2-Q4-26 at a normalized $35M/qtr (below Q1's print, since Fanapt/NEREUS/BYSANTI revenue is ramping): net cash at the PDUFA = 189.6 - 3(35) = $84.6M = $1.41/sh. Both legs below are marked to THAT figure, not to today's cash - a floor computed off 3/31 cash would be ~$1.75/sh too generous by December.

WIN LEG (approval 2026-12-12) = $8.90. Commercial base at 1.0x forward revenue, 2027E ~$300M -> $300M; plus imsidolimab GPP at $150M; plus net cash $84.6M = $534.6M / 60.1M sh = $8.89, call it $8.90. The $150M GPP mark is benchmarked to SPEVIGO (spesolimab, Boehringer) - the only approved GPP therapy and the SAME IL-36R mechanism, running roughly $150-250M globally. Imsidolimab arrives second into an ultra-rare indication (~3-5k diagnosed US patients), so I carry US peak at $80-120M and value it near 1.5x peak less launch risk. I did not underwrite the GLP-1-emesis (Thetis) or CMT2S (VCA-894A) options - both are early and undated.

LOSE LEG (CRL) = $3.60. Commercial base at a distressed 0.5x 2026 revenue (0.5 x $265M = $132.5M) + net cash $84.6M = $217.1M / 60.1M = $3.61. R:R AND EV. Upside 8.90 - 5.23 = $3.67; downside 5.23 - 3.60 = $1.63; R:R = 2.25:1. EV = 0.75(8.90) + 0.25(3.60) = $7.58, or +45% vs spot.

TAKEOUT LENS - APPLIED AND REJECTED, does NOT lift the win leg. Vanda has demonstrated acquirer interest: Future Pak bid $7.25-7.75/sh (March and May 2024, latter plus CVRs) and Cycle Pharma bid $8.00/sh cash valuing Vanda at ~$466M. All were rejected unanimously; Vanda adopted a poison-pill shareholder rights plan. Three reasons I refuse to mark those comps into fair value: (1) the board's own rejection rationale was that $7.25-7.75 was "a mere 7-15% premium to Vanda's cash balance of approximately $6.75 per share" - that cash balance is now $3.37/sh, so the arithmetic underpinning those bids is gone, and the bids are stale by two years; (2) founder-CEO Polymeropoulos plus the pill make the board a demonstrated structural blocker, not a seller; (3) the 2026 record M&A tape (37 biotechs >=$1B YTD, $216B) is a LATE-STAGE, commercially-ready, >=$1B-asset phenomenon - a $315M cap whose lead asset is second-to-market behind an entrenched Boehringer product is not the scarce asset that regime is bidding for. ALVO.thesis_summary: Alvotech resubmitted US BLAs for AVT05 (Simponi/Simponi Aria biosimilar) and AVT06 (Eylea 2mg biosimilar) on 2026-06-04 after the Jan-2026 facility-driven CRLs; the company states it "expects the FDA to conduct a six-month review," clocking an approval decision to roughly 2026-12-04. The defect that caused the CRLs was site-specific (deficiencies from the July-2025 Reykjavik pre-license inspection), and on 2026-07-29 the FDA closed its May-2026 re-inspection of that same facility as Voluntary Action Indicated (VAI) - i.e. no OAI, no approval-withholding classification. That is the single gating condition being cleared while the review clock runs, and it post-dates the board's 2026-06-08 valuation. Teva commercializes both assets. The equity is a thin stub over ~$1.53B debt and negative book equity (-$282M), so the December decision is genuinely binary at the equity level.
ALVO.kill_risk: The Q2 print on 2026-08-19 can spend the position before the catalyst ever resolves. Consensus Q2 revenue is $103M; with Q1 at $105.9M, H1 lands near $209M against unchanged FY guidance of $650-700M, requiring $441-491M in H2 - a 2.1-2.3x step-up off the H1 run-rate. A guidance cut re-rates the stub on leverage and cash burn, not on FDA odds, and there is precedent: the Jan-2026 CRL was accompanied by a slashed revenue guide and a 58% cut to adjusted EBITDA. The financing pattern corroborates stress rather than strength - $165M of equity issued at $3.75 (closed 06-17) followed by a $75M GoldenTree term loan just two weeks later (07-01). Separately, Celtic Lux (the founder vehicle) pledged 88,940,619 shares plus 7,007,321 depository receipts on 2026-06-26, ten days after buying 10.13M shares at $3.75; a pledged ~28% of the share count against a stock already near its 52-week low is a forced-sale vector that can break the $2.40 floor for reasons unrelated to the BLAs. Also note the December date is derived, not FDA-published (see dossier_note).

Board dossier was struck 2026-06-08, four days after the resubmission, and never picked up the clock.

ALVO.dossier_note:
MILESTONE DERIVATION - READ THIS BEFORE SIZING. The 2026-12-04 date is INFERRED, not published. I fetched both primary releases: the 06-04 resubmission PR says only "The company expects the FDA to conduct a six-month review of the resubmitted applications, consistent with the applicable regulatory timelines" and states NO target action date; the 07-29 VAI release also gives no timeline (CEO Lisa Graver: "We continue to work with the FDA to advance our recent Biologics Licence Applications towards approval"). The BsUFA Class 2 clock runs from FDA RECEIPT, not the announcement date, and FDA never publicly confirmed the resubmission class. Treat the milestone as a Nov-2026-to-Jan-2027 window centred on Dec 4, not a hard day-certain print. It is PENDING_HARD because the six-month statutory clock is binding, not because the day is known.

SCOPE - only AVT05 and AVT06 are on this clock. AVT03 (denosumab, Prolia/Xgeva) is NOT: the 06-04 PR states Dr. Reddy's "as applicant, is responsible for the U.S. regulatory submission," so its resubmission is separate and un-clocked. AVT16 (Entyvio biosimilar) had its BLA ACCEPTED 2026-06-08, a first-cycle review landing ~Q1-Q2 2027 - a later, separate event. Do not let the CRO fold AVT03/AVT16 into the December binary.

ARITHMETIC. The board's set reproduces exactly at the live price, so the errors are inputs, not math: win 6.00 / lose 2.75 / p 0.65 from 3.79 gives up +58.3%, down -27.4%, R:R 2.12, EV +28.3% - byte-matching the board's payoff 2.12 and ev_pct 0.283. Dilution bridge for the target: 293.0M shares (Q1) -> 338.2M today = +45.2M at $3.75; 45.2M x ($6.00-$3.75) = $102M / 338.2M = $0.30/sh; $6.00 - $0.30 = $5.70. Cross-check on the raise: 26,066,667 public x $3.75 = $97.8M, plus Celtic Lux 10,133,333 x $3.75 = $38.0M, plus ~$29M residual private placement = ~$165M aggregate as announced, ~44M shares - reconciles with the 45.2M implied by market cap. MARKET-IMPLIED PROBABILITY: at my two legs the tape is paying (3.79-2.40)/(5.70-2.40) = 42%. That 42% vs my 72% IS the entire edge - there is no valuation cushion underneath it. At the board's legs the implied number was 32%.

TAKEOUT LENS - NO LIFT APPLIED, and I want that on the record. ALVO is bio/pharma by label but does not fit the 2026 takeout regime, which is bidding clean late-stage/commercially-ready ASSETS. Alvotech is a levered manufacturing PLATFORM: $1.53B total debt (Q1 $1.457B + the $75M 07-01 GoldenTree term loan), negative book equity of -$282M, and its two lead US assets are already economically committed to Teva on commercialization. Logical strategics (Teva, Dr. Reddy's, Sandoz, Fresenius Kabi) are existing partners who get the economics without the balance sheet. I found NO named comparable takeout with date and value that would support a higher win leg, so per the provenance rule the target stays at $5.70. No milestone was created or extended from takeout speculation.

XBI CAVEAT CUTS THE OTHER WAY HERE. The standing warning - that a 5-year-high XBI makes market-implied win probabilities rich and old max-fear floors stale-low - does NOT apply to this name. ALVO has not participated: -64% over the trailing year, $3.79 against a 52-week range of $2.94-$9.25, 50-day $3.55 vs 200-day $4.47, and it just traded -8.0% on the session. This is an idiosyncratically broken name inside a strong tape, which is why a 42% market-implied probability is available at all - but it also means the $2.94 low is RECENT, not stale, and there is no sector bid propping the downside leg.

SKEPTIC PASS. Load-bearing claim tested: "VAI clears the path, so the December decision approves." Strongest refutation I can mount from the live record - VAI is not an approval commitment. The FDA still issued a Form 483 at the close of the May-2026 inspection, and VAI explicitly means objectionable conditions were FOUND but did not warrant regulatory action; it removes the site as a blocker without speaking to product-specific review issues in either BLA. Sequencing is favourable (resubmitted 06-04, inspection closed 07-29, decision ~Dec) but the company has now missed on this exact axis once, and Hagens Berman is investigating the adequacy of its manufacturing and regulatory-status disclosures. I held the lift to +7pp (0.65 -> 0.72) rather than the +10-15pp a clean facility-only read would justify. The residual risk that actually threatens the trade is not the FDA, though - it is the 08-19 Q2 print and the pledged founder stake; both are in kill_risk and both can resolve against the position months before the catalyst does.

IFF.thesis_summary: Signed, binding sale of IFF's Food Ingredients disposal group to CVC Capital Partners for ~$4.3bn EV / ~$3.8bn net cash proceeds, agreement dated 28 May 2026, guided to close by end of Q2 2027, outside date 28 May 2027, no financing condition, IFF retains an ~10% minority stake. The event is real, dated, unfired and idiosyncratic. The TRADE is not: on live 4 Aug 2026 primary numbers the deal-completes value of RemainCo (Scent + Taste + H&B) is ~$76/share against a $85.81 close, i.e. the event-win value sits ~11% BELOW the price. The repricing already happened — shares gapped $80.89 to $88.07 (+8.9%) on 5 Aug 2026 on the use-of-proceeds plan ($2.5bn buyback authorization, >$1bn debt paydown), and there has been no 8-K of any kind since 4 Aug. What remains to be bought is the ~10-month wait and the break-case left tail to ~$60, with the only route to upside being a re-rate to full Givaudan parity (15.8x), which would require the market to pay the category winner's multiple for a business running a 20.9% EBITDA margin and 2-4% cc sales growth.

Interim markers: $500m accelerated share repurchase guided for H2 2026 (NOT yet confirmed entered into — no 8-K between 4 Aug and 25 Aug 2026); Barclays Global Consumer Conference fireside chat 10 Sep 2026; $0.40 dividend ex-date 18 Sep 2026, payable 9 Oct 2026; Q3 results early Nov 2026.
IFF.kill_risk: The whole trade is one judgement: the RemainCo exit multiple. My $76 rests on 13.5x, and that number is a view, not a fact. Two credible refutations. (1) Parity: post-close IFF is a simplified Scent/Taste/H&B pure-play with leverage guided to 2.0-2.5x, 4-8% cc EBITDA growth and a buyback shrinking the count ~11% — exactly the shape the market has paid Givaudan multiples for. At Givaudan's live 15.8x my own arithmetic gives $91.8, ABOVE the $85.81 price, and the trade works. (2) Base-year: I deliberately anchor on FY2026 guidance and credit no 2027 organic growth. Rolling the base to a FY2027 EBITDA of ~$1.72bn (guidance-consistent 4-8% growth on the remediated base) at my own 13.5x gives ~$81/share — most of the gap to the tape closes without any re-rate at all. So "the event-win value is below the price" is true on a 2026 base at a Symrise-plus anchor and false on a 2027 base at Givaudan parity; a Director should treat my $76 as the conservative end of a $76-$92 band, not as a fact. Secondary risk: the ~$100m stranded-cost remediation could over-deliver (company guides substantially all eliminated within two years of close), which lifts the base further.

DEAL TERMS AS FILED. Transaction Agreement signed 28 May 2026 with CVC affiliates; ~$4.3bn EV; ~$3.8bn net cash proceeds subject to customary adjustments; IFF retains ~10% minority equity interest; conditions are regulatory approvals plus customary closing conditions with NO financing condition; outside date 28 May 2027; guided close "by the end of the second quarter of 2027" — reaffirmed verbatim on 4 Aug 2026. THE $520m RECONCILIATION (this overturns the weekly skeptic and matters in both directions). $4.3bn / $520m = 8.27x looks like a cheap sale, but $520m is a discontinued-operations figure and ASC 205-20 forbids allocating retained corporate overhead to discontinued operations. Add back the disclosed ~$100m that stays with IFF: standalone FI EBITDA ~$420m, $4.3bn / $420m = 10.2x — reconciling precisely to IFF's own "approximately 10x" of 29 May 2026. IFF is NOT selling cheap. The same fact cuts the other way for RemainCo: the $1.53-1.60bn continuing-ops guidance is ALREADY burdened by that ~$100m, so it is a conservative base that gets relieved post-close.

EVENT-WIN (DEAL CLOSES) — SoP. Base EBITDA: $1.565bn guidance mid + $0.067bn (crediting only the two-thirds of the $100m stranded cost the company guides to remove within one year) = $1.632bn. No 2027 organic growth credited — deliberately conservative. Multiple: 13.5x. Provenance for that anchor from live marks — Givaudan EV/EBITDA TTM 15.80x on 13.86% ROIC and a ~24% margin; Symrise EV/EBITDA TTM 11.08x on 7.80% ROIC. IFF RemainCo at a 20.9% margin and 2-4% cc growth does not earn Givaudan parity; 13.5x is ~240bp above Symrise for the Scent franchise and post-close simplification, ~230bp below Givaudan. EV = 13.5 x $1.632bn = $22.03bn. Plus retained ~10% FI stake at ~$0.20bn carrying value (marked at the CVC price, no control premium credited). Less pro-forma net debt $4.92bn (see arithmetic in discrepancies). Equity = 22.03 + 0.20 - 4.92 = $17.31bn. Shares at close = 257m less $500m ASR at ~$86 (5.8m) less $2.0bn at ~$90 (22.2m) = ~229m, an ~11% reduction. $17.31bn / 229m = $75.6 -> FAIR VALUE $76.

WHAT THE TAPE IS PAYING. Reverse the same bridge at $85.81: equity $19.65bn, plus net debt $4.92bn, less the stake $0.20bn = EV $24.37bn on $1.632bn = 14.9x. The market already pays RemainCo ~95% of the category winner's multiple and ~390bp above Symrise. That is the entire disagreement.

BREAK / LAPSE FLOOR. If CVC walks or a regulator blocks, consolidated EBITDA reverts to $1.565bn + $0.520bn = $2.085bn (this sum is arithmetically clean precisely because the stranded $100m already sits in the continuing-ops line). But a lapse IS the de-rate event — you do not keep the deal-era multiple in the deal-break case. At 10.0x, a shade below Symrise: EV $20.85bn less net debt $5.67bn = $15.18bn / 255m = $59.5. Independent confirmation: the observed 52-week low is $59.14, i.e. the tape has already priced a no-deal IFF at that level within the last twelve months. FLOOR $60. (The weekly skeptic's $63 credits 10.75x, which I regard as too generous for the scenario that destroys the multiple.)

R:R FROM $85.81. To fair value $76: MINUS 11.4%. To floor $60: MINUS 30.1%. There is no positive spread on either leg. Deal-close probability is high — I put it at ~90% (signed, no financing condition, financial-sponsor buyer, negligible horizontal overlap) — but a 90% chance of a ~11% loss and a 10% chance of a ~30% loss is a negative-expectancy shape, which is why win_prob is emitted null rather than 0.90: on an sop method a 0.90 in that field reads downstream as P(profit) and would invert the meaning of this dossier.

NOAA found the application in full compliance on 2026-04-30 and separately certified the USA B exploration application on 2026-05-28; the company guides the process to conclude before the end of Q1 2027. The event is idiosyncratic (a US federal permitting decision on its own facts) and unfired. Grant would re-rate the equity toward a fraction of the Aug-2025 NORI-D PFS NPV ($5.5B); denial or NEPA vacatur removes the US pathway and leaves cash plus a clouded ISA route. TMC.kill_risk: The permit slips past the guided Q1-2027 window and/or is granted-then-enjoined, while the ATM funds the wait - so the equity bleeds even on the winning path. DECK-MARK GATE - APPLIED, AND IT PASSES (this cuts in TMC's favor). Target rests on the Aug-2025 NORI-D PFS ($5.5B NPV, 51Mt probable reserves) plus the Initial Assessment ($18.1B, combined $23.6B). PFS LOM deck vs live tape: nickel deck $20,295/t vs spot ~$17,210/t (2026-08-03) = spot 15.2% BELOW deck; copper deck $11,440/t vs spot $6.6248/lb x 2204.62 = $14,606/t = spot 27.7% ABOVE deck; cobalt deck $56,117/t vs ~$55,000/t = roughly AT deck (held up by DRC export controls). SPOT-MARKED VARIANT using the issuer's OWN published NPV sensitivity (preferred over margin-scaling per the gate): TMC discloses 20% nickel decline takes NORI-D from $5.5B to ~$4.9B, i.e. -$0.6B per 20% nickel move; at 15.2% below deck that is -(0.152/0.20) x $0.6B = -$0.46B. Copper is a smaller line (70kt/y vs 97kt/y nickel) but 27.7% above deck, worth roughly +$0.3B on the same elasticity. Net spot-marked NORI-D NPV ~= $5.4B vs $5.5B deck, a ~2% haircut (~$0.23/sh undiluted). BOTH NUMBERS: deck $5.5B, spot-marked $5.4B. Conclusion: the deck is NOT materially stale - nickel weakness is very nearly fully offset by copper at ~$6.62/lb - so the deck price is not acting as a conditional cap here. My haircut to fair value is driven entirely by DILUTION and PERMIT PROBABILITY, not by the commodity tape. Spot-deck R:R is governed by the binary, not the deck.

XRN.thesis_summary: Chiron Real Estate (NYSE: XRN, ex-Global Medical REIT, 13.235M shares, $35.27) is mid-way through a self-directed recapitalization that converts a legacy net-lease medical-office book into a senior-housing operating (SHOP) platform. Announced 2026-05-06: $425M of Silverstone SHOP communities, a $100M delayed-draw convertible perpetual preferred led by Maewyn Capital, ~$200M of asset sales, a new debt facility, a 36% monthly dividend cut to $0.16, and withdrawal of 2026 guidance. Two legs have already fired: The Landing + The Riviera closed 2026-06-01 for $249M, and seven IRFs were recapitalized into an 85/15 JV with a US public pension fund at a $217M aggregate valuation on 2026-06-30. What remains forward is the third community, The Pinnacle North Bethesda, at ~$176M, company-guided to close October 2026 (broadened to Q4 2026 in the 06-01 release), plus the balance of the ~$200M disposition program. The equity is a sum-of-parts on depreciated real estate: management's own disclosure that the $249M of SHOP equals ~14% of the portfolio by gross real estate assets implies ~$1.78B of gross cost against $1.238B of depreciated assets and $668.6M of net debt, so roughly $540M (~$41/share) of accumulated depreciation sits between carrying value and cost. The market caps the legacy book at ~76% of gross cost; marking it at 85% and holding the two 2026 transacted assets at their own arms-length prices gets to ~$44/share. XRN.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that the legacy net-lease medical book is worth materially more than its depreciated carrying value, and the live record pushes back hard. XRN.dossier_note:
CATALYST. Real, idiosyncratic, partly spent, and only soft-dated. The board's forced-seller framing does not survive the live record (see discrepancies). Program announced 2026-05-06 alongside Q1 results: acquire three Silverstone senior-housing communities for $425M aggregate; fund with a $100M delayed-draw convertible perpetual preferred led by Maewyn Capital Partners, ~$200M of asset sales, a new debt facility, and a 36% cut in the monthly dividend to $0.16; 2026 guidance withdrawn. FIRED legs: The Landing + The Riviera (292 homes - 169 IL / 89 AL / 34 memory care, Washington DC MSA) closed 2026-06-01 for $249M, funded with cash on hand, revolver capacity and the Maewyn investment; seven inpatient rehabilitation facilities were recapitalized into a JV with a US public pension fund at a $217M aggregate valuation on 2026-06-30, the investor taking 85% of the equity. UNFIRED leg: The Pinnacle North Bethesda, MD, ~$176M under definitive purchase agreement, guided to October 2026 on 2026-05-06 and restated as Q4 2026 on 2026-06-01. Nearer information event, NOT named as the milestone because it is one day out and unpriced by this dossier: Q2 2026 results 2026-08-05 after close, call 2026-08-06 09:00 ET (company release 2026-07-16), consensus -$0.235 EPS on $37.64M revenue - the first print carrying SHOP economics and the IRF deconsolidation, and the plausible venue for guidance reinstatement.

VALUATION - SoP, arithmetic. All axes are mine; the board emitted nulls. Anchor is the company's own portfolio-mix disclosure in the 2026-06-01 release: the $249M of closed SHOP equals ~14% of the portfolio by gross real estate assets, so gross real estate cost = 249 / 0.14 = $1,778.6M. Cross-check against the same release's pro forma statement that Pinnacle plus ~$200M of sales takes SHOP to ~25%: (249 + 176) / (1,778.6 + 176 - 200) = 425 / 1,754.6 = 24.2%. Consistent, so the $1.78B gross figure is reliable. Against $1,238.0M of depreciated total assets at 2026-03-31, that implies ~$540M (~$41/share) of accumulated depreciation between carrying value and cost - the NAV wedge.

Components, pro forma post-06-30: (a) SHOP Landing + Riviera at their own 2026-06-01 arms-length price, $249M; (b) retained 15% of the IRF JV at the pension fund's own 2026-06-30 mark, 0.15 x 217 = $32.6M; (c) legacy net-lease medical book at gross cost 1,778.6 - 249 - 217 = $1,313M, marked at 85% of cost = $1,116M to reflect 2026 MOB cap rates sitting above the 2016-2022 acquisition cap rates. GAV = 249 + 32.6 + 1,116 = $1,397.2M. Less net debt $668.6M, preferred at carrying $124.1M, minority interest $20.4M = $584.1M common equity / 13.235M shares = $44.13, taken as fair_value_target $44.00 (+24.8% vs $35.27). Net debt is held at the 2026-03-31 figure because the pro forma legs roughly offset ($249M out for SHOP against ~$184M gross in from the 85% JV sale) and the JV-level debt is not visible in the record.

Sensitivity on the only free variable, the legacy mark: 90% of cost = $49.09/share; 85% = $44.13; 75% = $34.22. At 75% the discount disappears entirely - the market's current $35.27 is capitalizing the legacy book at ~76% of gross cost. That single assumption carries the whole thesis, which is why it is the kill_risk.

downside_floor $28.42 = depreciated common book value per share at 2026-03-31: ($500.211M total stockholders' equity - $124.106M preferred) / 13.235M shares, equivalent to marking the legacy book at ~67% of gross cost. It is an audited number, and a REIT mid-pivot with withdrawn guidance and a freshly cut dividend is exactly the profile that trades to and through book. -19.4% vs spot. R:R at these axes is roughly 1.3:1 - thin for an event sleeve.

No win_prob emitted: this is a NAV-discount SoP, not a binary. No takeout lens applied - REIT, not bio/pharma. No deck-mark gate - no commodity linkage; the SoP rests on two 2026 arms-length property transactions plus a cost-basis haircut, not on a price deck.

CONSTRAINTS ON THIS WORK. The SEC 10-Q (2026-05-07) and the Q1 8-K exhibit both returned HTTP 403, so I could not read portfolio NOI, cap rates, the JV debt stack, or the Maewyn conversion price directly. FMP's REIT line mapping is self-contradictory - Q1-26 EBITDA $23.714M plus G&A $5.089M annualizes to ~$115M of NOI, while revenue $38.064M less implied property opex ($38.904M cost of revenue - $14.827M D&A = $24.08M) annualizes to only ~$56M. A 2x spread makes a cap-rate NAV indefensible, which is why the SoP is built on transacted marks and the company's own gross-asset mix statistic instead. Treat the legacy-book mark as a judgement, not a measurement.

UK and Swiss decisions are also guided to 2H 2026, with Menarini targeting German and UK launch in Q4 2026. (2) PREVAIL cardiovascular outcomes trial interim analysis to be conducted in Q4 2026 with results expected in Q1 2027, reaffirmed in the 5 August 2026 Q2 release and unchanged from the 7 May 2026 Q1 release. If the trial does not stop for efficacy, completion is anticipated by end-2027. Event count and stopping boundary are undisclosed. RUBENS Phase 3 topline (about 300 patients, type 2 diabetes or metabolic syndrome) is guided to year-end 2026. No US regulatory event exists: no FDA application has been submitted, there is no decision date, and management states only that it is working with the agency on how the interim affects filing timelines.
NAMS.thesis_summary: NewAmsterdam is a one-asset company. Obicetrapib is an oral CETP inhibitor with three positive Phase 3 LDL-lowering trials in hand (BROADWAY, BROOKLYN, TANDEM), a CHMP positive opinion dated 23 July 2026, and a European Commission approval decision due in the second half of 2026. That approval is close to a formality once CHMP has spoken, so it is largely in the price and it is not what the trade resolves on. The trade resolves on the PREVAIL cardiovascular outcomes trial, whose interim analysis runs in Q4 2026 with the result reported in Q1 2027. If PREVAIL shows an outcomes benefit, obicetrapib becomes a cheap oral non-statin LDL agent with hard event data, opens a US filing, and turns on the Menarini European royalty in full. If it misses, the company is a shell with cash and a niche European royalty. Neither branch is dated to a day and the interim's most likely single outcome is "continue," which resolves nothing.
NAMS.kill_risk: The modal path is a non-event that costs a year. The Q1-2027 milestone is an interim look, not a topline, and interims usually return "continue." In that branch nothing resolves, the stock likely de-rates on the absence of an early efficacy stop, the true binary moves to end-2027, and the company burns roughly another $180 million getting there. That is a duration mismatch a 12-month event sleeve cannot hold. Separately, the win leg rests on a US peak-sales figure for an asset with no US filing: if PREVAIL does stop early for efficacy, the effect estimate is an early-stopped one, and regulators and payers routinely discount those, so the branch that pays fastest is also the branch that pays least. Both the target and the floor are therefore softer than a two-point binary makes them look.
