NAMS.dossier_note:
FACTS VERIFIED LIVE. Price $26.85, market cap $3.14bn, 116,903,979 shares outstanding (10-Q for period ended 30-Jun-2026, filed 5-Aug-2026). Cash, equivalents and marketable securities $678.3m at 30-Jun-2026, down from $707.3m at 31-Mar and $728.9m at 31-Dec-2025. Q2 operating cash burn $39.2m, Q2 net loss $64.1m. CHMP positive opinion adopted 23-Jul, announced 24-Jul-2026. EC decision guided 2H26 and NOT yet issued. PREVAIL interim Q4-26, result Q1-27, completion end-2027 if no efficacy stop. RUBENS topline by year-end 2026. Menarini European licence: EUR 115m upfront plus EUR 27.5m committed R&D, up to EUR 863m in clinical, regulatory and commercial milestones, tiered double-digit royalties from the teens to the mid-twenties on European net sales across 32 countries.

FLOOR REBUILT, board $14 -> $6.00. Cash at the point failure is confirmed: forward burn runs about $45m per quarter once launch preparation and RUBENS are loaded on top of the $39m Q2 run-rate. Failure confirmed at the Q1-2027 interim leaves $678.3m less three quarters of burn, about $543m, or $4.65 per share. Failure confirmed at end-2027 instead leaves six quarters of burn, about $408m, or $3.49 per share. The interim's modal answer is "continue," so weight the later date more heavily: 40/60 gives about $3.95. Add roughly $0.50 per share of European regulatory milestone cash from Menarini, which is close to certain now that CHMP has spoken and arrives in either branch, giving $4.45 of cash. Add the European royalty stub: after an outcomes miss the European product survives on its LDL label but uptake collapses, so call peak European net sales EUR 100-200m at a low-teens royalty, capitalised at six times and discounted, worth $1.00-$1.70, take $1.25. Add $0.25 for the patent estate and residual pipeline. Total $5.95, call it $6.00, with $6.00-$7.00 as the honest range. I will not credit a third-party bid for the shell: torcetrapib, dalcetrapib, evacetrapib and anacetrapib were none of them sold, licensed or revived after their outcomes trials, so the buyer of a failed CETP shell wants only the cash, which is already leg one. The board's $14 double-counts that leg.

IMPORTANT QUALIFIER ON THE FLOOR, and the CRO should read this before using the drawdown number. The $6.00 is terminal wind-down value in the miss branch, realised at end-2027 in most paths. It is NOT where the stock trades on a "continue" interim in Q1-2027. On a non-event the stock falls but stays far above $6. So the headline -77.7% is the eventual loss in the losing branch, not the drawdown the position experiences at the milestone.

TARGET REBUILT, board $60 -> $54.00. Bottom-up on the win branch. Europe: with outcomes data in hand call European peak net sales EUR 1.0-1.5bn at a blended royalty near 20%, so EUR 200-300m a year, at six times and time-discounted about $0.9-1.3bn, plus roughly $250m of discounted remaining Menarini commercial milestones out of the EUR 863m pool, so $1.15-1.55bn, or about $11.50 per share. United States: peak sales $2.0bn, which is where published consensus sits, at three times peak is $6.0bn, haircut 25% for launch, reimbursement and execution risk gives $4.5bn, or $38.50 per share. Rest of world partnering $2.00 per share, half the record's $4.00. Alzheimer's and Lp(a) at zero, consistent with the record's own treatment of them. Net cash at the event $4.65, though a US launch consumes it. Sum $56.65, less about 5% for option exercises running near $11m a quarter and a plausible win-case raise, gives $53.90. Call it $54.00. The board's $60 requires four times peak on the US franchise and the full $4.00 rest-of-world leg, and lands above the $58 street high.

DO NOT USE STREET TARGETS AS A CROSS-CHECK ON WIN PROBABILITY. On my pair, a $51.33 blended consensus implies a 94% win probability, which is nonsense. Sell-side biotech targets are effectively pure win-case numbers with no failure branch, so their proximity to my $54 is confirmation that $54 is a sane win-leg value, and tells you nothing about odds.

ODDS. At $26.85 against $54.00 and $6.00 the market implies (26.85-6.00)/(54.00-6.00) = 43.4%. I set 0.50, below the board's 0.55. Against the bull: the CETP class is 0 for 4 in outcomes trials, and PREVAIL's own disclosure that MACE rates are running below plan is a power problem, not a comfort, because a low event rate can make the trial miss even if the drug works. For the bull, and the skeptic's "0 for 4" framing understates this: dalcetrapib and evacetrapib failed because they raised HDL without meaningfully lowering ApoB, whereas anacetrapib, the one class member that did lower LDL, did hit its outcomes trial at a 9% relative risk reduction. Obicetrapib lowers LDL-C by roughly 30% on top of statin and also lowers Lp(a), and the LDL-to-MACE relationship is among the best-validated in cardiology. The record on LDL-lowering CETP inhibitors is 1 for 1, not 0 for 4. That earns a coin flip, not better, because the expected effect size is modest and needs events the trial is not generating fast enough.

RESULT. EV = 0.50 x 54.00 + 0.50 x 6.00 = $30.00 against $26.85, so about +11.7%, not the board's +41%. Payoff is +101% against -77.7%, a ratio of 1.30, not 2.32. On a 43% market-implied probability against my 50%, the edge is about 7 points of probability. That is a thin, honest edge, not the asymmetry the board carried.

TAKEOUT LENS, and it does not lift the target. Obicetrapib would be the first new oral non-statin LDL mechanism with outcomes data in a decade, and cardiometabolic is crowded with acquirers: Novartis (Leqvio adjacency, an oral would complement a twice-yearly injectable), AstraZeneca (cardiorenal franchise), Merck (owns the anacetrapib institutional knowledge) and Lilly (lepodisiran, muvalaplin). But I have no named, dated, valued lipid or CV takeout comparable to cite, so per the comp-provenance rule the win-leg target stays at $54.00 with zero takeout credit. There is also a structural reason a bidder waits: the entire class history says buy after outcomes, not before, and Merck's own anacetrapib experience is the case study. Takeout here is undated optionality sitting on top of the readout, not a milestone, and I have not created or extended one from it. On the regime caveat: XBI at a five-year high cuts against this entry rather than for it. A 43% implied win probability struck at a five-year sector high is not a fear price, so there is no stale-low floor print to exploit here. The corrected floor is a fundamental wind-down number, not a max-fear mark, and the regime does not rescue it.

PVLA.thesis_summary: Palvella Therapeutics (Wayne PA, 14.34M shares, $2.02B cap) has one asset that matters: QTORIN 3.9% rapamycin anhydrous gel for microcystic lymphatic malformations (mLM), a rare vascular malformation with ~30,000 diagnosed US patients and ZERO FDA-approved therapies. The pivotal event already fired: Phase 3 SELVA read out positive 2026-02-24 (n=49 ITT, mean +2.13 on the mLM-IGA at Week 24, p<0.001; key secondary and all four additional secondaries also p<0.001), and the stock is up ~620% off the $36 low. What is STILL unfired is the regulatory conversion: FDA granted rolling review 2026-06-22, Palvella submitted the first NDA module 2026-06-29, and guides to COMPLETING the 505(b)(2) NDA in 2H 2026 with potential US approval and launch in 1H 2027. Breakthrough Therapy and Fast Track are in hand; $261.9M cash at 3/31/26 after the upsized $230M February raise fully funds submission, launch build-out, and the 2H26 Phase 3 start in cutaneous venous malformations (75,000 US patients) plus the Phase 2 LOTU angiokeratoma readout (2H 2027). The remaining edge is therefore regulatory/commercial conversion of an already-de-risked efficacy package, not a data event - and the milestone is a guided half-year window, not a binding date.
PVLA.kill_risk: SELVA is a SINGLE-ARM, BASELINE-CONTROLLED Phase 3 whose primary endpoint is an unblinded clinician-rated global assessment (mLM-IGA). There is no vehicle arm, so neither placebo/attention effect nor natural fluctuation of a chronic lesional disease is quantified, and the assessor was not blinded to treatment. That is exactly the package FDA can meet with a CRL demanding a controlled confirmatory trial - which would reset the timeline 2-3 years and take the equity to roughly the downside floor. Compounding it: the 2043-protected IP and $100-200k/yr pricing frame collide with compounded topical sirolimus, already used off-label at vascular-anomaly centers, so payer step-edits could cap real uptake well below the ">$1B US peak" bull frame even on approval. Secondary residual: the near-term event is only NDA COMPLETION inside an undated 2H26 window - a slip into 2027 is a de-rating (roughly the $109 200-day / pre-June levels) without any thesis break, so the position can bleed on timing alone with no falsifying news.

GFL.thesis_summary: GFL is the ACQUIRER in the C$6.4B enterprise-value arrangement to buy SECURE Waste Infrastructure at C$24.75/SECURE share (80% GFL stock / 20% cash), so closing delivers accretion and a re-rate, not a premium to GFL holders. The event is real, forward-dated and unfired: FTC cleared 2026-05-05, SECURE holders approved in May, the court issued its final order 2026-05-28, and the SOLE outstanding condition is Canadian Competition Bureau clearance, under review since 2026-05-01 with no decision announced as of 2026-08-25 (verified: no GFL SEC filing since 2026-07-31). The arrangement-agreement outside date is 2026-11-01; management's 2026-07-29 language is "still targeting closing for the latter part of 2026." Valuation is a pro-forma EV/EBITDA sum-of-parts, not a spread. Re-derived from filed numbers: pro-forma Adj EBITDA C$2,865M (GFL FY26 guidance C$2,290M raised 07-29 + SECURE C$550M reaffirmed at the top of C$520-550M on 07-29 + C$25M disclosed run-rate synergies), pro-forma net debt C$11,495M, 434.1M shares, giving US$50.50 at a generous 14.6x peer anchor. The debate record's US$57 does not survive: it rested on a 9-10x purchase multiple that appears in no company document — GFL's own 2026-04-13 deck puts the deal at ~11.9x 2026E and ~11x post-synergy against a GFL standalone ~13.1x, so this is a modest currency arbitrage, not three to four turns. The separate take-private process (special committee confirmed 2026-07-29, reported level ~US$50) is undated optionality that caps at roughly the same number as the fundamental target, with a founder holding 25%+ of the vote who says he will roll 100% of his equity — it supports the floor more than it lifts the ceiling.
GFL.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that Competition Bureau clearance is close to a formality — which is exactly what the live tape encodes: SECURE trades C$24.18 against a mark-to-market mixed-election value of C$24.227 at GFL.TO C$57.44, a 0.19% discount, i.e. essentially zero deal risk priced. The live record refutes that complacency. This same regulator litigated SECURE's last major merger in this exact market — the Commissioner proved a substantial lessening of competition in 136 of 143 markets in SECURE/Tervita, the Tribunal ordered divestiture of 29 facilities (2023-03), the Federal Court of Appeal upheld it, and the Supreme Court denied leave (2024-02) — and the Bureau separately challenged GFL's own Terrapure acquisition in 2021. The review has now run ~3.8 months against Dovigi's own 3-5 month estimate, consistent with a deep supplementary-information-request process rather than an early no-action letter. A remedy package that carves facilities out of SECURE would cut both the C$550M EBITDA and the C$25M synergy and drops the target below US$50 while the shares carry the full 11.9x purchase price. Second residual: even on clean clearance the win requires a re-rate toward mid-teens peers, which my own build says is unearned — pro-forma leverage lands at 4.0x on the Adj EBITDA basis (3.9x on management's Run-Rate convention) versus the guided "low-to-mid 3s," so GFL's discount to WM/RSG/WCN is arguably a fair charge for balance-sheet and oilfield-waste cyclicality, not a closable gap. Third: US$50.50 IS the sell-side consensus (US$50.95 mean, US$52.00 median) — there is no differentiated upside in this number, and because GFL is the acquirer there is no contractual backstop, no break fee receivable in a regulatory block, and GFL owes up to C$20M in expense reimbursement.

Second, the last capital-allocation move made under exactly this thesis destroyed value: Sinclair accumulated 9.9% of Scripps and bid $7/share in December 2025; the board unanimously rejected it and SSP now trades at $3.32, marking that stake roughly 50%+ below the bid Sinclair itself put on the table.
